requested_scope: pg_net 0.19.5 Production-version contract versus 0.20.4 Dev-version contract, plus PostgreSQL 17 BEFORE INSERT / RETURNING semantics.
version_assignment_source: Production 0.19.5 / Dev 0.20.4 supplied by Root from earlier evidence; no project access was made in this review.

trace.finding: The actual worker calls consume_request_queue and then insert_curl_responses.
The queue consumer deletes selected rows with RETURNING q.id first, reads that first SPI column as int64, and passes that same value into init_curl_handle.
init_curl_handle assigns the received id directly to cdata->id.
The CurlData pointer is retained as CURLOPT_PRIVATE and recovered through CURLINFO_PRIVATE on completion.
The transport-failure path inserts its received id as the first INT8 parameter into net._http_response.id.
The transport-success path inserts cdata->id as the first INT8 parameter into net._http_response.id.
Both completion paths consume the same preserved CurlData identity.

pg_net_0_19_5.meaning: Identity is preserved when this upstream worker writes a response; this does not promise successful delivery, retention, or exactly-once effects.

trace.finding: The queue DELETE still returns q.id first; get_request_queue_row reads it as int64 into RequestQueueRow.id.
RequestQueueRow and CurlHandle both retain the identifier as int64.
The worker passes each get_request_queue_row result directly into init_curl_handle.
On completion the same private handle is passed into insert_response.
insert_response puts handle->id into vals[0], which supplies net._http_response.id.

sources.finding: A row-level BEFORE INSERT trigger may return a modified row; that returned row is the row inserted.
RETURNING observes the row as modified by triggers.

postgresql_17_semantics.conclusion: Provided the BEFORE INSERT trigger fires and returns NEW, INSERT ... RETURNING id receives the final trigger-assigned id. The reviewed pg_net worker subsequently preserves the stored queue id as response id.
assumptions: The correct BEFORE INSERT row trigger actually fires.
The trigger returns the modified NEW row rather than NULL.
No later trigger changes the id again.
postgresql_17_semantics.sql_api_definitions: Root reports their exact installed V2 hashes already checked; this review did not execute SQL or independently re-query their installed definitions.
